item.content:encoded:
CorpsAfrica is accepting applications for its Development Associate position in Washington, DC, offering an opportunity for early-career professionals interested in fundraising, donor relations, nonprofit management, communications, community development, and international development.

The full-time position offers an annual salary of $55,000 to $60,000 and is designed for a professional who can combine strong communication and relationship-building abilities with careful donor data management, prospect research, event support, and cross-departmental collaboration.

The Development Associate will work closely with CorpsAfrica’s Donor Relations Manager and contribute to efforts to expand and strengthen the organisation’s donor base. The successful candidate will support donor cultivation and stewardship, fundraising campaigns, donor events, prospect research, financial reconciliation, and the maintenance of accurate donor information.

The position is based in Washington, DC, with a hybrid arrangement requiring two days per week, although remote work may also be considered. The successful applicant should also be willing to travel domestically and internationally for up to 20% of their time.

Applications must be submitted by September 30, 2026.

About CorpsAfrica

CorpsAfrica is an organisation focused on empowering young Africans to lead community-driven development initiatives within their own countries and across the African continent.

The organisation was founded in 2011 by former Peace Corps Volunteer Liz Fanning. The idea behind CorpsAfrica emerged from her experience with young Moroccans who expressed an interest in becoming Peace Corps Volunteers so they could contribute to communities in their own country.

At the time, the Peace Corps opportunity was available to Americans serving internationally. CorpsAfrica was subsequently developed around a different model: creating opportunities for young Africans to serve as volunteers and contribute to locally led development across Africa.

CorpsAfrica launched its first programme in Morocco in 2013. Since then, the organisation has expanded significantly across the continent.

According to CorpsAfrica, its programmes have operated across countries including:

  • Morocco
  • Senegal
  • Malawi
  • Rwanda
  • Kenya
  • South Africa
  • The Gambia
  • Ghana
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Ethiopia

The organisation has expanded to 11 countries and has an ambitious long-term objective of eventually reaching all 54 African countries.

Hundreds of CorpsAfrica Volunteers have participated in the organisation’s programmes, supporting more than 800 community projects.

These projects have covered a broad range of community priorities, including:

  • Building wells
  • Constructing schools
  • Developing roads
  • Establishing irrigation systems
  • Creating literacy programmes
  • Supporting vegetable farming
  • Supporting livestock farming
  • Advancing community-led development initiatives

The organisation’s broader approach centres on enabling communities and local changemakers to identify priorities and participate actively in designing and implementing solutions.

About the CorpsAfrica Development Associate Position

The Development Associate will support CorpsAfrica as the organisation continues to develop its donor community and strengthen its culture of philanthropy.

Rather than concentrating exclusively on fundraising outreach, the position combines donor-facing relationship management with operational fundraising responsibilities.

The successful candidate will work closely with the Donor Relations Manager to cultivate, steward, and strengthen relationships with donors.

An important part of the position involves ensuring donors receive timely and professional communication while maintaining accurate records of their engagement with CorpsAfrica.

The Development Associate will also help identify and qualify potential donors, support donor relations strategies, assist with fundraising events and campaigns, and track and analyse donor activity.

This means candidates should be comfortable moving between communication-oriented responsibilities and detailed administrative and data-management work.

Position Details

Key information about the vacancy includes:

  • Position: Development Associate
  • Organisation: CorpsAfrica
  • Location: Washington, DC
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Classification: Exempt
  • Experience level: Entry level
  • Salary: $55,000–$60,000 annually
  • Working arrangement: Hybrid, two days per week, with remote work considered
  • Reports to: Donor Relations Manager
  • Travel: Domestic and international travel of up to 20%
  • Application deadline: September 30, 2026

Key Responsibilities of the Development Associate

The Development Associate will have responsibilities spanning donor stewardship, database management, fundraising operations, prospect research, events, communications, and financial coordination.

1. Donor Acknowledgements and Stewardship

One of the central responsibilities of the position is supporting positive and professional relationships between CorpsAfrica and its donors.

The Development Associate will be responsible for processing donor receipts and acknowledgements promptly.

Timely donor acknowledgement is an important component of nonprofit fundraising because it ensures supporters receive appropriate recognition for their contributions while helping the organisation maintain strong relationships with its donor community.

The Associate will also help maintain high-quality donor information within Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud.

2. Donor Data Management

Accurate data management will be another important component of the position.

The Development Associate will:

  • Enter donor information into relevant systems
  • Update existing donor records
  • Verify donor information
  • Maintain accurate fundraising data
  • Support reporting requirements
  • Help ensure fundraising records remain organised and reliable

The role will support both fundraising and finance teams, making attention to detail particularly important.

Candidates with experience using donor databases or customer relationship management systems may therefore have relevant experience for this position.

3. Cross-Departmental Collaboration

The Development Associate will not work exclusively within one team.

Instead, the successful candidate will collaborate with colleagues across different departments and geographical locations.

This includes working with:

  • Communications teams
  • Development teams
  • Regional teams
  • Finance colleagues
  • Other stakeholders involved in donor engagement

This collaboration will help support donor engagement initiatives, fundraising activities, events, reporting, and organisational campaigns.

Because CorpsAfrica operates internationally, applicants should be comfortable collaborating across different cultures and time zones.

4. Supporting Donor Events

Events are another component of CorpsAfrica’s donor engagement strategy.

The Development Associate will assist with the planning and execution of regional donor events.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Event logistics
  • Donor outreach
  • Event coordination
  • Communications
  • Follow-up activities
  • Supporting the overall donor experience

Candidates with previous experience in event planning, fundraising events, nonprofit events, stakeholder engagement, or similar activities may find this aspect of the role particularly relevant to their background.

5. Prospect Research

Expanding an organisation’s donor base requires identifying individuals and organisations that may have an interest in supporting its mission.

The Development Associate will support the Donor Relations Manager with researching and qualifying major donor prospects.

Tools used for this work may include:

  • WealthEngine
  • Salesforce

Prospect research can involve reviewing potential supporters, maintaining accurate information, helping determine whether prospects align with the organisation’s fundraising priorities, and supporting future cultivation strategies.

Experience with WealthEngine is preferred but is not listed as an absolute requirement.

6. Finance Coordination

The Development Associate will also collaborate closely with CorpsAfrica’s finance team.

This work will help ensure fundraising records and financial systems remain aligned.

Responsibilities will include supporting accurate reconciliation and reporting between fundraising and financial systems.

Because donor contributions have both fundraising and financial reporting implications, accurate coordination between these systems is an important part of maintaining organisational accountability.

Educational Requirements

Applicants should hold a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline.

CorpsAfrica specifically identifies the following fields:

  • Marketing
  • Business
  • Communications
  • Nonprofit management
  • Related disciplines

Applicants whose degrees are in closely related fields may also qualify, depending on the relevance of their education and professional experience.

Professional Experience Required

Candidates should have approximately one to three years of relevant professional experience.

Relevant experience may include areas such as:

  • Fundraising
  • Donor relations
  • Development
  • Event planning
  • Nonprofit administration
  • Communications
  • Donor database management
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Related fields

As the position is described as entry level, it could be particularly relevant to early-career professionals who have already developed foundational experience and now want to strengthen their careers in nonprofit development and fundraising.

Communication and Organisational Skills

Strong written and verbal communication abilities are required.

The Development Associate will interact with donor information, support donor communications, coordinate across departments, and assist with events. Clear and professional communication will therefore be important.

Applicants should also possess excellent organisational skills.

The successful candidate must be capable of managing multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.

This may require balancing responsibilities such as:

  • Processing donor acknowledgements
  • Updating donor records
  • Conducting prospect research
  • Supporting fundraising campaigns
  • Assisting with events
  • Coordinating with finance
  • Responding to internal requests
  • Supporting donor reporting

Candidates should therefore be comfortable working in an environment where priorities may overlap.

Technology and Database Skills

Applicants should be proficient in Google Workspace.

Experience with donor databases and fundraising technology is preferred.

CorpsAfrica specifically mentions experience with:

  • Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud
  • WealthEngine

These platforms can support donor relationship management, fundraising operations, prospect research, data analysis, and reporting.

Although previous experience with these tools is preferred, the vacancy does not state that candidates without such experience are automatically excluded.

Ability to Work Across Cultures and Time Zones

CorpsAfrica operates across multiple countries, meaning the Development Associate may collaborate with colleagues and stakeholders working in different cultural and geographical environments.

The organisation is therefore looking for someone who is:

  • Highly collaborative
  • Comfortable working across cultures
  • Able to communicate effectively with different teams
  • Comfortable working across different time zones
  • Capable of balancing operational and relationship-focused responsibilities

These capabilities are particularly relevant given CorpsAfrica’s expanding presence across the African continent.

Travel Requirements

Applicants must be willing to travel both domestically and internationally.

Travel may account for up to 20% of the position.

Prospective applicants should consider this requirement before applying, particularly if they have restrictions that would make regular domestic or international travel difficult.

Commitment to CorpsAfrica’s Mission

Beyond education and technical skills, CorpsAfrica is looking for a candidate who demonstrates a genuine commitment to the organisation’s mission and values.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate alignment with areas including:

  • Youth leadership
  • Participatory community development
  • Impact evaluation
  • Transparency
  • Accountability

Understanding CorpsAfrica’s mission will be particularly important when preparing the cover letter.

Applicants should consider explaining not only why they have the technical qualifications for the role, but also why CorpsAfrica’s approach to community development and youth leadership is meaningful to them.

Salary and Working Arrangement

The Development Associate position offers an annual salary range of $55,000 to $60,000.

The role is classified as a full-time, exempt position.

It is based in Washington, DC, with a hybrid working arrangement involving two days per week. CorpsAfrica also states that remote work may be considered.

Candidates interested in remote work should nevertheless carefully review the position’s travel and collaboration requirements.

U.S. Work Authorisation Requirement

There is an important eligibility requirement that prospective international applicants should note before preparing an application.

Applicants must be legally authorised to work full-time in the United States.

CorpsAfrica also states that candidates should not require employment sponsorship.

Therefore, applicants who would require CorpsAfrica to sponsor them for U.S. employment authorisation should take this restriction into consideration before applying.

Equal Opportunity Employment

CorpsAfrica identifies itself as an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The organisation encourages applications from individuals regardless of:

  • Age
  • Gender
  • Race
  • Ethnicity
  • Sexual orientation
  • Marital status
  • Physical ability
  • Other legally protected characteristics

Selection should therefore be based on the requirements and qualifications associated with the position rather than these personal characteristics.

Application Requirements

Candidates interested in the Development Associate position must submit an application through CorpsAfrica’s JazzHR recruitment platform.

Applicants are required to provide a résumé and cover letter.

The cover letter should clearly demonstrate how the applicant’s qualifications and experience relate to the Development Associate role.

Applicants should use the cover letter as an opportunity to connect their professional background with responsibilities such as donor relations, fundraising, event coordination, data management, communications, stakeholder engagement, and nonprofit development.

The online application also requests information including:

  • First and last name
  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • Address
  • Résumé
  • Cover letter
  • References and their contact information
  • A description of experience relevant to the position

Applicants should ensure all required fields are completed before submitting their application.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because CorpsAfrica states that only complete applications will be considered, applicants should carefully review their materials before submission.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate relevant experience rather than relying on general statements.

For example, candidates with fundraising experience may highlight their involvement in donor communications, fundraising campaigns, donor databases, prospect research, stewardship, or reporting.

Candidates with event-planning experience could describe responsibilities such as:

  • Coordinating event logistics
  • Managing invitations
  • Communicating with stakeholders
  • Supporting event delivery
  • Conducting post-event follow-up
  • Managing multiple deadlines

Applicants with database or administrative experience should consider demonstrating their ability to maintain accurate records and work with detailed information.

Experience using Salesforce, WealthEngine, or comparable platforms should also be clearly identified.

What to Highlight in Your Cover Letter

The cover letter is specifically requested to illustrate qualifications relevant to the position.

Applicants may therefore want to structure their cover letter around several major themes.

Relevant professional experience

Explain how previous positions, internships, volunteer experiences, or projects have developed skills relevant to fundraising, donor relations, event planning, communications, or nonprofit management.

Data and technology skills

Mention relevant experience with Google Workspace, Salesforce, WealthEngine, donor databases, CRM platforms, spreadsheets, reporting systems, or other related tools.

Communication abilities

Provide examples demonstrating strong written and verbal communication, particularly where the work involved donors, clients, partners, stakeholders, or colleagues.

Organisational skills

Explain how you have managed multiple responsibilities, deadlines, projects, events, or stakeholders simultaneously.

Cross-cultural collaboration

Where applicable, highlight experience working with international teams, diverse communities, or colleagues across different locations and time zones.

Mission alignment

Explain why CorpsAfrica’s work in youth leadership and participatory community development aligns with your professional interests and values.

Applicants should ensure that all claims made in their application materials accurately reflect their actual experience.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the CorpsAfrica Development Associate position is September 30, 2026.

Prospective candidates should aim to prepare and submit their materials before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Only complete applications will be considered.

APPLY NOW

Why This Position May Appeal to Early-Career Development Professionals

The CorpsAfrica Development Associate role combines several important areas of nonprofit development work within one position.

Rather than concentrating on only one fundraising function, the successful candidate will gain exposure to donor stewardship, prospect research, database management, fundraising operations, events, finance coordination, and cross-departmental collaboration.

For someone building a career in nonprofit development or international development, this combination can provide practical experience across both the relationship-building and operational sides of fundraising.

The international nature of CorpsAfrica’s work also means the successful candidate will be supporting an organisation focused on locally led development and youth leadership across Africa.

Conclusion

The CorpsAfrica Development Associate 2026 opportunity offers an early-career professional the chance to contribute to the fundraising and donor engagement operations of an organisation working to advance locally led community development across Africa.

Based in Washington, DC, with a hybrid arrangement and remote work potentially considered, the full-time role offers an annual salary of $55,000–$60,000 and combines donor relations, fundraising operations, event support, prospect research, data management, and finance coordination.

Applicants should have a relevant bachelor’s degree, approximately one to three years of applicable experience, strong communication and organisational abilities, proficiency with Google Workspace, and an ability to collaborate effectively across cultures and time zones. Experience with Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud and WealthEngine is preferred.

Candidates must also be legally authorised to work full-time in the United States without requiring employment sponsorship and should be willing to travel domestically and internationally for up to 20% of their time.

Most importantly, CorpsAfrica is looking for an individual who can demonstrate a commitment to its mission and values, including youth leadership, participatory community development, impact evaluation, transparency, and accountability.

Interested candidates should prepare a complete application, including a résumé and a cover letter that clearly demonstrates their relevant qualifications and experience.

Application deadline: September 30, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Women’s Developmental Leadership Program 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from eligible Pacific women who are Australia Awards scholars studying at Australian universities and tertiary institutions.

Key Information at a Glance

Program: Women’s Developmental Leadership Program
Target group: Pacific women Australia Awards scholars
Number selected: Up to 30 participants annually
Program period: 2026–2027
Application opens: 21 September 2026
Application deadline: 25 October 2026
Leadership intensives: February and September 2027
Location: Australia and Pacific region
Funding/Support: Coaching, residential leadership intensives, real-issue challenges and workplace internship opportunities
Eligibility: Citizens of listed Pacific countries who meet the Australia Awards scholar requirements

Each year, up to 30 Pacific women Australia Awards scholars are selected to participate in the program, which aims to strengthen women’s leadership capabilities, develop individual leadership styles, and build connections across the Pacific and Australia.

Through developmental leadership training, coaching, residential intensives, real-issue challenges and workplace internships, participants gain practical skills and networks to support lasting change in their communities, countries and region.

What Is the Women’s Developmental Leadership Program?

The Women’s Developmental Leadership Program supports Pacific women Australia Awards scholars to establish the foundations of developmental leadership, strengthen their leadership practice and develop regional and country-based connections.

The program also provides continuing support to alumni after they return to the Pacific, helping them apply developmental leadership approaches to real-world challenges.

Participants have access to several program offerings designed to build leadership knowledge, practical experience, confidence and professional networks.

Program Benefits and Opportunities

1. Bespoke Coaching

Participants and alumni can access one-on-one issues-based and collective ontological coaching sessions.

These coaching opportunities provide a supportive space to strategically work through barriers that may prevent participants from reaching their leadership potential.

2. Residential Leadership Intensives

The program includes two week-long residential leadership intensives.

These intensives enable participants to:

  • Build deep connections with other Pacific women leaders
  • Learn from prominent Pacific and Australian leaders
  • Explore different approaches to leadership
  • Test leadership concepts in their own contexts
  • Develop their personal leadership style
  • Strengthen regional networks

The two intensives will take place in February 2027 and September 2027.

3. Real Issue Challenges

Participants identify and address real-life developmental issues affecting their communities, countries and regions.

These challenges provide an opportunity to apply leadership learning and skills to practical situations while embedding developmental leadership approaches.

Additional opportunities to expand these initiatives may be available through the Leadership Fund.

4. Workplace Internships

Selected participants and alumni may receive support to design, seek and secure work placements and internships across Australia and the Pacific.

These placements are intended to help participants:

  • Build professional skills
  • Develop new networks
  • Gain practical experience
  • Increase readiness for leadership roles
  • Strengthen connections between Australia and the Pacific

 

Key Program Dates

Date Program Activity
21 September 2026 Applications open
25 October 2026 Applications close at 11:59 PM Australian Eastern Daylight Time
25 October – 16 November 2026 Selection process and applicant notification
16 November – 1 December 2026 Registration and onboarding
2 December 2026 Online induction/orientation
28 January – 4 February 2027 Intensive 1 – Outward Bound Australia, Tharwa, ACT
20 – 26 September 2027 Intensive 2 – Clear Mountain Lodge, Brisbane, QLD

Eligibility Requirements

To apply for the Women’s Developmental Leadership Program, applicants must:

  • Identify as a woman
  • Be enrolled as an Australia Awards scholar at an Australian university or tertiary institution during the first semester of the calendar year
  • Be available to commence the program in Australia in February 2027
  • Commit up to 15 days of face-to-face participation across the two residential intensives in February and September
  • Have access to the internet
  • Be a citizen of an eligible Pacific country

View the official application requirements

Apply Now:
Submit an application for the Women’s Developmental Leadership Program

Eligible Pacific Countries

Citizens of the following countries and territories are eligible to apply:

  • Cook Islands
  • Federated States of Micronesia
  • Fiji
  • French Polynesia
  • Kiribati
  • New Caledonia
  • Naoero
  • Niue
  • Palau
  • Papua New Guinea
  • Republic of Marshall Islands
  • Samoa
  • Solomon Islands
  • Tokelau
  • Tonga
  • Tuvalu
  • Vanuatu
  • Wallis and Futuna

Women’s Developmental Leadership Program Application

Applications for the Women’s Developmental Leadership Program 2026–2027 opened on 21 September 2026 and close on 25 October 2026 at 11:59 PM Australian Eastern Daylight Time.

Eligible Pacific women Australia Awards scholars interested in developing their leadership capabilities, expanding their networks and contributing to positive change in their communities are encouraged to review the application requirements before applying.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the 2027–2029 Mundus MAPP cohort, offering prospective students the opportunity to pursue a two-year Erasmus Mundus Master’s Programme in Public Policy across leading European universities, with a limited number of prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarships available to outstanding applicants from both EU and non-EU countries.

The programme is designed to provide scholarly education and practical training for future academic and policy leaders in the public, private and non-profit sectors, with a particular focus on understanding how political institutions, processes and public policies operate from the global political economy through national and local levels, including European engagements.

Key Details

  • Programme: Erasmus Mundus Master’s Programme in Public Policy – Mundus MAPP
  • Cohort: 2027–2029
  • Duration: 24 months
  • Study format: Full-time, in-person
  • Study locations: Austria, Spain, the Netherlands and the UK, depending on the selected mobility track
  • Scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship
  • Maximum EMJM scholarship: €33,600 over 24 months
  • Monthly scholarship contribution: €1,400
  • Tuition fee: €13,000 per academic year / €26,000 for the full programme
  • Scholarship application deadline: 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
  • Scholarship: No separate scholarship application is required.

 

What is the Mundus MAPP Programme?

Mundus MAPP is an Erasmus Mundus Master’s Programme in Public Policy delivered by a consortium of four institutions.

The programme combines a common core of policy studies with specialised mobility tracks. Approximately 60% of the curriculum is common to all students, while 40% is delivered through track-specific modules. The programme also includes study visits, internships and research work across the two years.

Mundus MAPP is a full-time in-person programme that allows students to tailor their learning experience through the selection of a mobility track. Students are exposed to different European academic traditions and policy contexts through study visits and internships.

The programme has a strong practical component, including internships, spring courses/study trips and case-study-based teaching. These activities are intended to help students observe real-world policymaking, interact with practitioners, apply theoretical knowledge to practical policy problems, conduct research and build professional networks.

Four Mundus MAPP Study Tracks

Applicants may apply to one of four mobility tracks:

1. CEU-IBEI Track – Global Public Policy

This track focuses on the policy process at the international and global level, including international organisations and global policy regimes.

Students study at Central European University (Private University) in Vienna, Austria, in Year 1, before continuing at Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals (IBEI) in Spain in Year 2.

2. CEU-York Track – European Public Policy

This track focuses on policy analysis, policymaking and problem-solving in the European Union, its member states and neighbourhood countries.

Students study at Central European University in Vienna in Year 1 and continue at the University of York in the UK in Year 2.

3. ISS-IBEI Track – Political Economy and Development

This mobility track combines study at the International Institute of Social Studies (ISS) in the Netherlands and IBEI in Barcelona, Spain, with a focus on political economy and development.

4. ISS-York Track – Governance and Development

This track combines study at ISS in the Netherlands and the University of York in the UK, focusing on governance and development.

The four tracks offer different substantive focuses while maintaining a common core of policy studies.

Important: Applicants may apply for only one mobility track.

Erasmus Mundus Scholarship – What Does It Cover?

The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship will be offered to outstanding applicants from both within and outside the EU.

A limited number of EMJM scholarships are awarded to the highest-ranked applicants for the duration of the programme.

The scholarship is calculated at €1,400 per month, corresponding to a maximum scholarship amount of €33,600 over 24 months. The monthly contribution is intended to assist students with travel, visa, installation, subsistence and other costs.

EMJM scholarship recipients also receive a full tuition-fee waiver.

Additional financial support may be available for students with individual needs depending on the level of disability/support required.

Institutional Scholarships

In addition to the EMJM scholarships, the Mundus MAPP Consortium will offer one Institutional Scholarship per study track.

Recipients receive a 50% tuition fee waiver at the Year 1 and Year 2 institutions. The Institutional Scholarship does not include a stipend.

Costs Not Covered by the EMJM Scholarship

Applicants should budget carefully because the EMJM scholarship does not cover:

  • Study Visit: approximately €600–€1,000
  • Winter School: approximately €600–€1,000
  • Travel and visa costs between the student’s home country and consortium countries
  • Travel costs when moving to the Year 2 university.

The programme also strongly encourages applicants to seek external funding because only a small number of applicants will receive scholarships.

Mundus MAPP Financial Aid and Scholarships

Official Mundus MAPP website

Who Can Apply?

Mundus MAPP is open to European and third-country national students.

Applicants must meet the programme’s minimum admission requirements.

Academic Requirements

Applicants must have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree comprising at least three years of study from a recognised university or higher education institution.
  • At least Class 2.1/Upper Second, where applicable.
  • A minimum GPA of 3.17/4.0 or equivalent.
  • Applicants are required to provide their GPA on a 4.0 scale.

Candidates with degrees in the social sciences or equivalent are normally given preference.

Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree in Natural Sciences or Engineering are not eligible to apply.

Applicants who already hold a Master’s degree must also meet the required academic standard at Master’s level. The programme notes that priority for scholarships is given to students who have not yet had the opportunity to study in a Master’s degree programme.

Mobility Requirement

Physical mobility is compulsory for all enrolled students.

Students must complete two study periods in two different countries, with each study period comprising a minimum of 30 ECTS. Both countries must be different from the student’s country of residence at the application/enrolment stage.

Compulsory mobility periods cannot be replaced by virtual mobility. Applicants will also need to provide proof of residence before enrolment.

This is particularly important when selecting your mobility track.

English Language Requirements

Mundus MAPP does not require an English language certificate from citizens of several countries, including Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, South Africa, Tanzania, The Gambia, Liberia, the UK, USA, Canada, Australia and others, provided they have completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree taught exclusively in English.

For other applicants, accepted tests include:

  • TOEFL iBT: 95 or above
  • IELTS Academic: 7 or above
  • Cambridge C2 Proficiency: C2 or above
  • Cambridge C1 Advanced: C1 or above
  • Pearson PTE Academic: 76 or above
  • Duolingo English Test: 130 or above.

Important update for ISS applicants

Applicants considering the ISS-IBEI or ISS-York tracks should pay particular attention to the Dutch visa requirements.

For the 2027–2029 cohort, some applicants admitted to an ISS track may need to provide additional proof of English proficiency for their Dutch visa. The programme states that these are visa requirements, not admissions requirements.

Applicants from Ghana and several other previously exempt countries may apply without a test result, but admission to the ISS tracks may be conditional until an accepted English test is submitted. The test must be provided no later than six weeks after receiving the official offer.

Work Experience Is Not Required

Work experience is not an eligibility requirement, although candidates with relevant work experience may be considered favourably.

This means the programme can be relevant to both recent graduates and applicants who have already developed professional experience in public policy, development, government, international organisations, civil society, research or related areas.

What Documents Do You Need?

Applicants should prepare the following:

1. Online Application Form

There are four application forms corresponding to the four mobility tracks. Applicants may apply for only one track.

2. Two Recommendation Letters

Applicants must provide two official letters of recommendation, preferably with at least one from an academic.

Referees receive an email after the application is submitted and have seven days to upload their recommendations. Applicants are advised to monitor the Applicant Portal and remind referees of the deadline.

References sent by email, fax or regular post are not accepted.

3. Academic Records

Applicants must upload electronic versions of their higher education academic records, including:

  • Official English translation of the Bachelor’s degree transcript
  • Official English translation of the Bachelor’s degree diploma/degree certificate
  • Relevant Master’s degree documents, where applicable.

4. Curriculum Vitae/Resume

The CV should include a list of publications, if applicable.

5. Statement of Purpose

The statement of purpose must be no more than 500 words and should highlight:

  • Your reasons for applying to Mundus MAPP
  • Your research interests
  • Relevant academic and work experience
  • Future career plans
  • The study track to which you are applying.

The programme specifically notes that, because of the high number of applications, longer statements will not be considered.

6. Proof of English Proficiency

Where required, applicants must submit the relevant English language test as part of the online application. Late submission of test scores is not permitted.

What Should You Know About the Application Process?

Admissions to Mundus MAPP are centrally administered by Central European University Private University.

Applications must be submitted to CEU PU through the specified online application process. It is not possible to apply to Mundus MAPP through another consortium university.

Candidates complete the online application and upload the required supporting documentation.

If you want to be considered for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship, you simply indicate your interest in the online application form.

There is no separate scholarship application.

How to Apply – Mundus MAPP

2027–2029 Mundus MAPP Application Deadlines

Applicants should carefully select the deadline that applies to their circumstances.

December 1, 2026 – 23:59 CET

This is the key deadline for applicants who:

  • Wish to be considered for financial aid/scholarships, or
  • Are applying early as self-funded students.

The first-round decisions, including EMJM scholarship decisions, will be available in the Applicant Portal on April 14, 2027.

April 15, 2027 – 23:59 CET

Deadline for non-EU/EEA residents who do not wish to be considered for financial aid.

July 1, 2027 – 23:59 CET

Deadline for EU/EEA residents who do not wish to be considered for financial aid.

For scholarship applicants, the important date to remember is December 1, 2026.

View the official Mundus MAPP Admissions Calendar

How Are Scholarships Awarded?

The scholarships are awarded based on academic merit.

Applicants who submit their application by the December 1, 2026 scholarship deadline will be asked in the online portal to indicate their interest in a potential scholarship.

Because the number of scholarships is limited, applicants are strongly encouraged to explore additional funding opportunities.

Important Advice for Prospective Applicants

Start preparing early

Do not wait until the deadline to begin collecting documents. Recommendation letters, official translations, academic records and English-language tests can take time.

Choose your mobility track carefully

Your application is for one specific mobility track, so applicants should review the curriculum, countries, institutions and specialisation associated with each track before submitting their application.

Pay attention to the 500-word limit

Your statement of purpose should be no more than 500 words. Use the limited space to clearly explain your motivation, academic and professional background, research interests, career plans and preferred track.

Contact your referees early

Recommendation letters must be uploaded within seven days after the application is submitted. Ask your referees in advance and make sure they know to check their spam folders for the automated email.

Read the ISS visa requirements carefully

If you are considering an ISS-IBEI or ISS-York track, check the additional Dutch visa-related English requirements before submitting your application.

What Can Students Expect From the Programme?

Mundus MAPP aims to develop graduates who can:

  • Critically analyse policy issues and develop holistic perspectives on European and global governance.
  • Evaluate public policies and policy instruments using quantitative and qualitative methods.
  • Conduct research, analyse data and produce scientifically sound reports.
  • Provide expert advice to decision-makers in national and international settings.
  • Design and participate in the delivery of public policies across different sectors and institutional settings.

The programme therefore combines academic study, policy analysis, research, practical experience and international mobility.

Mundus MAPP 2027–2029: Application Checklist

Before submitting your application, make sure you have:

☐ Selected one mobility track
☐ Checked that you meet the academic requirements
☐ Confirmed that you meet the mobility requirements
☐ Prepared your academic transcripts and degree certificate
☐ Arranged two recommendation letters
☐ Prepared your CV/resume
☐ Written a statement of purpose of 500 words or fewer
☐ Checked the English language requirements
☐ Prepared official English translations where required
☐ Indicated your interest in financial aid if applying by December 1, 2026
☐ Checked the application deadline for your applicant category
☐ Submitted the complete online application
☐ Followed up with your referees after submission.

Official Mundus MAPP Admissions Checklist

Apply for the Mundus MAPP 2027–2029 Cohort

Applications are currently open for the 2027–2029 Mundus MAPP cohort.

Applicants seeking consideration for the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship should submit their application by:

December 1, 2026 at 23:59 CET

The scholarship provides up to €33,600 over 24 months, calculated at €1,400 per month, together with a full tuition-fee waiver for successful EMJM scholarship recipients.

item.content:encoded:
Looking to build your knowledge and skills in sustainability, climate action, sustainable development and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)? The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) offers a range of free online courses covering topics including climate change, sustainable development, SDG budgeting, climate negotiations, women’s leadership, official statistics, resilience and the 2030 Agenda.

These free UNITAR courses provide an opportunity for learners, professionals, policymakers, students and development practitioners to strengthen their knowledge and skills in areas that are increasingly important for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

Free UNITAR Sustainability and Sustainable Development Courses

Below is a list of 18 free sustainability courses from UNITAR covering sustainable development, climate action, SDG implementation, data, governance and related topics.

1. Anticipatory Governance: Systems Thinking & Strategic Foresight for SDG-Aligned Integrated Planning

This course explores systems thinking, strategic foresight and anticipatory governance to support integrated planning aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gw4p_XMB

2. Inclusive Learning Design

Learn about inclusive learning design and approaches that can help make learning environments more accessible and responsive to diverse learners.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dt8bfH2w

3. Practical Methods to Implement and Uphold the FPOS for Producers

This course focuses on practical approaches to implementing and upholding the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPOS) for producers of official statistics.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/g5hAWCRz

4. Introduction to Official Statistics

Gain an introduction to official statistics, including their importance for evidence-based policymaking, development planning and informed decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gmszNJHX

5. Insurance and the Sustainable Development Goals

Explore the relationship between insurance and the Sustainable Development Goals, including how insurance can contribute to sustainable development and resilience.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gj5aMhXg

6. Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action

This course focuses on developing skills to strengthen women’s leadership in climate action and support greater participation in climate-related decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eE5saH5D

7. Strengthening Stakeholder Engagement for the Implementation and Review of the 2030 Agenda

Learn approaches for strengthening stakeholder engagement in the implementation and review of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dw7gix7

8. Introduction to Sports for Climate Action

Discover how the sports sector can contribute to climate action and support broader efforts to address climate change and advance sustainable development.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eVggDGWj

9. SDG-Aligned Budgeting

Learn about SDG-aligned budgeting and how public budgets can be connected to national sustainable development priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gHe26r_z

10. Geospatial Information Technology in Fragile Contexts

Explore the use of geospatial information technology in fragile contexts and its potential applications for development, planning and decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dFUpd6UR

11. Mainstreaming the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

This course examines approaches to mainstreaming the 2030 Agenda and integrating sustainable development priorities into policies, plans and development processes.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dpdj2PEH

12. Art and the Stewardship of the Ocean

Explore the relationship between art, ocean stewardship and sustainable development, highlighting creative approaches to raising awareness about ocean-related challenges.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eyAuKgv2

13. Infrastructure Asset Management for Sustainable Development

Learn about infrastructure asset management and its importance for sustainable, resilient and effective infrastructure development.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gxAfSSv4

14. Mastering International Climate Negotiations: All You Need to Know

Develop knowledge of international climate negotiations, including key concepts and processes relevant to global climate policy and action.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eqUemTwB

15. Environmental SDG Indicators

Learn about environmental indicators for the Sustainable Development Goals and how data and indicators can support sustainable development monitoring and decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dMG9U7Nv

16. Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPOS) and Their Relevance for Policymakers

Understand the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPOS) and their relevance to policymakers, evidence-based policy and effective decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dCHDsJaT

17. Strengthening Climate Adaptation and Resilience

This course explores climate adaptation and resilience, helping learners understand approaches to strengthening resilience to climate-related risks and impacts.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eRFamQcv

18. Understanding Data and Statistics Better – for More Effective SDG Decision Making

Develop a better understanding of data and statistics for SDG decision-making and learn how reliable evidence can support more effective sustainable development policies and actions.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/d9My2QH

Who Can Take These Free UNITAR Courses?

These courses may be particularly useful for:

  • Students and recent graduates
  • Young professionals
  • Development practitioners
  • Sustainability professionals
  • Climate and environmental practitioners
  • Policymakers and government officials
  • Researchers and academics
  • NGO and civil society professionals
  • Professionals working on the SDGs
  • Anyone interested in climate action and sustainable development

Why Take Free UNITAR Online Courses?

UNITAR’s online learning opportunities can help learners develop knowledge relevant to some of the world’s most pressing development challenges. Topics covered across these courses include climate change, sustainability, sustainable development, the SDGs, the 2030 Agenda, climate adaptation, resilience, data and statistics, governance and policy.

For students and professionals, completing relevant online courses can also be a useful way to expand knowledge, develop professional skills and strengthen a CV or professional profile.

Start Learning Online

If you are looking for free online sustainability courses, free UN courses, climate change courses, SDG courses or sustainable development training, explore the UNITAR opportunities above and check the individual course pages for the latest information on eligibility, registration, course dates and completion requirements.

Bookmark this page and share it with students, young professionals and development practitioners who may benefit from these free learning opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27, offering Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni the opportunity to connect, share knowledge and skills, build professional networks, and support development impact.

The CSC’s Mentoring Programme connects Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni to support knowledge and skills development, and provide practical tools to support Scholars in achieving development impact.

Why Take Part in the CSC Mentoring Programme?

Commonwealth Scholars will have the opportunity to learn from an experienced Commonwealth Alumnus, and gain valuable insights, personalised guidance, and practical advice to help maximise their development impact.

Mentees will also be able to build professional connections, receive support in adapting to life and study in the UK, and develop their professional confidence for future career opportunities.

Commonwealth Alumni play a key role in shaping a new Scholar’s journey and future impact. As Mentors, they will provide advice on developing new skills and knowledge and applying this learning to drive development impact after the scholarship.

The programme offers a rewarding opportunity for Mentors to enhance their mentoring and leadership skills, expand their networks, and share their expertise and experiences within the wider CSC community.

The Mentoring Programme runs for one year from December 2026 until December 2027, with sessions taking place online.

How to Apply for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27

All eligible Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni will receive full information about the programme and how to apply in September 2026.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is 23:59 (BST) on Sunday 11 October 2026.

You can find out more about the opportunity and read testimonials from previous participants on the CSC Mentoring Programme page.

For more information about the eligibility criteria, please read the CSC Mentoring Programme – FAQs.

If you have any questions about the CSC Mentoring Programme, or how to apply, please contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk for more information.

CSC Mentoring Programme

The Mentoring Programme enables Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni to connect and inspire each other to create real-world impact.

By matching new Scholars with experienced Alumni working in fields relevant to their studies, the programme offers a unique opportunity for one-on-one guidance and practical insight, helping scholars turn academic knowledge into meaningful action after their Scholarship.

How Does the Programme Work?

Applications open in August each year, with the programme running from the following January – December (one year cycle).

Successful applicants are matched with a Mentor or Mentee whose background and aspirations closely align with their own, ensuring a personalised experience.

Your mentoring partnership will progress through five stages, each designed to help you achieve key milestones and make the most of your time together. You’ll be supported throughout the year with programme handbooks, regular communications, and skills development resources, giving you the tools to succeed at every stage.

To help you get started and build a productive mentoring partnership, you will be invited to join online information sessions at the beginning of the programme. There’ll also be lively virtual meet-ups where you can connect with other Mentees and Mentors, share your experiences, and build best practice.

Who Can Join the CSC Mentoring Programme?

Commonwealth Master’s and Doctoral Scholars

Become a Mentee and unlock the chance to turn your academic achievements into real-world impact. Through personalised guidance from a Commonwealth Alumnus, you’ll learn how to translate your skills and knowledge into tangible development outcomes back home and gain invaluable insights on navigating life and studies in the UK.

As a Mentee, you’ll receive tailored support to help you excel both academically and professionally, with advice on everything from adapting to a new culture to building the employability skills that will set you apart after your Scholarship.

Commonwealth Alumni

By becoming a Mentor, you’ll play a crucial role in guiding and inspiring the next generation of Scholars, helping them to develop the skills and confidence needed to create meaningful change in their home countries and fields.

As a Mentor, you’ll have the rewarding opportunity to share your knowledge and offer practical advice, supporting a Scholar as they navigate their studies and future career. You’ll also expand your own skillset, enhancing your leadership, communication, and mentoring abilities.

You will receive information via email when applications open. If you have any questions, you can read our Frequently Asked Questions page or contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

Why Should I Take Part?

To find out what inspired previous Mentors and Mentees to join the programme, read the testimonials below.

“The Mentoring Programme exceeded my expectations in most areas, particularly in understanding how to apply my studies for development impact and learning from my Mentor’s expertise as a Commonwealth Scholar. My Mentor provided invaluable insights into practical applications of my field, helping me align my academic goals with real-world challenges. My Mentor also offered excellent professional development advice, which has been instrumental in shaping my career plans. While the advice on living and studying in the UK was helpful, it aligned closely with what I had anticipated. Overall, the programme has been a transformative experience.”

2023 Mentee from India

Commonwealth Alumni who have significant professional experience post-Scholarship can volunteer to become a Mentor.

As a Mentor, you will have the opportunity to share your expertise to support a new Scholar in developing appropriate skills and knowledge to achieve development impact post-Scholarship and provide advice on how these skills can applied in their home country or home country region. Through the programme, you will develop mentoring and professional skills, such as leadership, communication, and knowledge-sharing.

Image of Commonwealth Scholars discussing

“The CSC Mentoring Programme provided a well-structured platform for personal and professional growth, offering both the resources and guidance necessary to foster meaningful Mentor-Mentee relationships. The programme enabled me to enhance my mentoring skills, while also giving me the opportunity to make a positive impact on my Mentee’s academic, professional, and social development. The collaborative aspect was particularly rewarding, as it allowed me to share knowledge and learn from my Mentee’s fresh perspectives. I feel that the programme successfully met its objectives, and I would recommend it to fellow Alumni seeking to develop as Mentors.”

2023 Mentor from Pakistan

How Does the Programme Work?

Applications open in September 2025 and pairings will be announced in November 2025. The programme runs for one year from December 2025 to December 2026.

Image of Commonwealth Scholars discussing

Successful applicants are matched in a one-to-one mentoring pairing based on their application responses.

The programme consists of 5 stages, which help guide pairs through important milestones to achieve their goals for the programme. Mentees and Mentors will have access to resources including programme handbooks and a range of skills development resources. All participants will have the opportunity to attend virtual information sessions at the start of the programme and virtual meet-up sessions to connect with fellow Mentees and Mentors and share best practice.

How Can I Apply?

All eligible Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni will receive full information about the programme and how to apply in September 2024. You can find out more about the by reading Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

If you have any questions about the programme, contact the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

CSC Mentoring Programme Eligibility

Who Can Apply to Take Part in the Programme?

Mentees

  • All 2026 Commonwealth Scholars studying in the UK
  • Continuing PhD Scholars

Mentors

  • All Commonwealth Alumni who have studied in the UK and have at least one year post-Scholarship
  • Current Mentors may apply to take part for another year

What Does It Mean If I Apply and Am Not Paired?

There are a greater number of eligible Commonwealth Alumni than incoming Scholars. This typically means the programme receives more applications for Mentors than Mentees and as such, not all Mentor applications can be paired.

Pairings are made based on application responses across a number of areas, including: pairing country preference; Mentor and Mentee subject and/or field of study; topic area; key words; motivations for becoming a Mentor/Mentee; and the professional experience of a Mentor.

Will I Receive Feedback on My Application?

We are unable to provide feedback on individual applications. We encourage all unsuccessful applicants to apply to the programme in future, or submit a request to volunteer for any similar opportunities by contacting the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

About the CSC Mentoring Programme Pairing

Will I Have the Same Mentor/Mentee Throughout the Programme?

Yes, you will have the same Mentor/Mentee for the duration of the year-long cycle.

Will I Be Paired With a Mentor/Mentee From the Same Subject Area?

Pairings are based on a range of factors, including home-country or cross-country pairing preference, subject and/or field of study, topic area, key words, motivations for joining the programme, and the Mentor’s professional experience.

While subject area and field of study are considered, they are not the primary criteria for pairing. The CSC aims to create pairings that support meaningful knowledge-sharing, professional development, and mentoring relationships.

Where possible, applicants will be matched using the information provided in their applications. However, direct matches, where a Mentor and Mentee studied the same subject or attended the same institution, are uncommon and are not the primary aim of the programme.

Are All Pairings Successful?

During the programme, there is the possibility that not all pairings will continue for the full duration of the programme. In these situations, the Alumni Team will terminate the pairing. Reasons for unsuccessful pairings vary and some are outlined below:

  • Mentor/Mentee has not submitted their agreement form confirming participation
  • Mentor/Mentee is unable to continue due to personal, professional, or other unforeseen commitments
  • Mentor/Mentee mutually agree that the pairing is not suitable

The CSC cannot guarantee an alternative pairing if a mentoring pairing ends early. However, participants are encouraged to seek out alternative means of support through CSC activities.

What Should a Mentor/Mentee Do If There Is a Disagreement?

You should refer to the section on constructive feedback in Mentoring Programme Handbooks available on the CSC website. The information on constructive feedback will support pairs in having healthy and positive mentoring conversations.

If you still have any concerns about how to go about this or are unable to reconcile differences, please contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

Can a Mentor Engage a Third Person or Expert to Help Their Mentee Regarding a Specific Need?

The CSC Mentoring Programme is based on a one-to-one relationship between a Mentor and Mentee. However, where appropriate, a Mentor may recommend or facilitate contact with a third party who can provide specialist advice or expertise relevant to the Mentee’s needs.

Before introducing a third party, the Mentor must obtain the consent of both individuals and must not share any personal information, including names or contact details, without their prior agreement.

Can Mentors Proof-Read Essays?

Mentors can provide guidance, look at sections of work, but should not edit whole chapters or essays, as this is not the purpose of a Mentor.

If a Mentee Goes to the Same University as Their Mentor, and Is Doing a Similar Course, Can They Share Notes or Past Exams Papers?

This practice can be frowned upon in some UK institutions. Mentees should contact their course coordinator if they wish to view or access these materials.

Meeting Your Mentor/Mentee

Who Should Initiate the First Introduction?

The Mentor should make the first contact by email and introduce themselves to their Mentee. This initial introduction helps establish the mentoring relationship, set expectations, and begin planning future communication.

You can read guidance on the type of information to share in initial communications in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks.

Is a Physical Meeting Between Mentors and Mentees Allowed?

The CSC Mentoring Programme is designed primarily as a virtual programme, as Mentors and Mentees are often based in different countries during the Scholarship period.

If a Mentor and Mentee happen to be in the same location and both wish to meet in person, they may do so at their own discretion. Any in-person meeting should be arranged by mutual agreement, take place in a safe and appropriate setting, and comply with any relevant local guidance or regulations (for instance, COVID regulations).

Neither Mentor nor Mentee should feel obligated to meet in person, and either party may decline such a meeting if they are uncomfortable doing so.

What Is the Minimum Commitment to Meet Every Month?

The minimum commitment of engagement is two hours every month. You can organise this time in whatever way works best for your goals and time commitments.

Can I Meet With My Mentor/Mentee More Than 2 Hours in a Month?

Yes, you can. You will both need to agree meetings and time commitments.

What If I Do Not Hear From My Mentor/Mentee?

When contacting your Mentor/Mentee, keep in mind that they may have reasons to not respond immediately. The reasons could include important work/study deadlines, travel, illness, or other personal reasons. Always provide a sufficient deadline for them to respond by and if you still fail to hear back, notify the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

CSC Mentoring Programme Goal Setting

What Type of Goals Can I Set?

It is important to set clear goals at the start of the cycle so you know what support your Mentor/Mentee needs to provide, and you understand what you can ask them about. Goals may relate to academic, professional, and personal growth. Please refer to the SMART goals framework in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks.

Should Mentors Set Goals?

Yes. The CSC Mentoring Programme is a two-way learning experience, and Mentors are encouraged to set goals for their own development, as well as support their Mentee in achieving theirs.

As a Mentor, consider what you hope to gain from the experience, the skills you would like to develop, and what you would like to learn from your Mentee.

Examples of Mentor goals include: developing mentorking, leadership and professional skills, building meaningful connections, expanding knowledge of a different sector, country, or professional context, building meaningful connections within the Commonwealth community.

Please refer to the SMART goals framework in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks.

After the CSC Mentoring Programme

Will I Get a Certificate for Participating in the Programme?

Participants who complete the full mentoring cycle and complete the final feedback survey will receive a certificate confirming their participation.

Can Mentors and Mentees Stay in Touch After the Programme?

We encourage Mentors and Mentees to discuss whether they would like to keep in contact following the end of the formal programme and you should discuss this during the final stage. It is important to remember that the dynamics of this relationship may be different post-programme.

Apply for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27

The CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27 provides Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni with an opportunity to build meaningful professional connections, exchange knowledge, strengthen mentoring and leadership skills, and support development impact.

The application deadline is 23:59 (BST) on Sunday 11 October 2026.

For further information, visit the CSC Mentoring Programme page and read the CSC Mentoring Programme – FAQs.

For questions about the programme or how to apply, contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

item.content:encoded:
The Brunel University of London and China Scholarship Council (CSC) PhD Scholarship 2027/28 offers academically outstanding Chinese students an opportunity to pursue a fully funded PhD at Brunel University of London in the United Kingdom.

For the 2027/28 intake, 20 full scholarships are available for PhD studies commencing in October 2027 or January 2028. The scholarships are jointly supported by Brunel University of London and the China Scholarship Council.

The funding package includes full tuition fees for up to 48 months, a living-cost stipend including medical insurance, one international round-trip economy-class airfare between China and the UK, and reimbursement of one-off visa application fees.

About the Brunel University and CSC PhD Scholarship

The scholarship programme is designed to provide academically strong Chinese students with the opportunity to undertake doctoral research at Brunel University of London.

The 2027/28 programme offers:

  • 20 full PhD scholarships
  • Study at Brunel University of London
  • Scholarships available across all disciplines
  • PhD programmes commencing in October 2027 or January 2028
  • Up to 48 months of tuition fee coverage
  • Living-cost stipend from CSC
  • Medical insurance
  • International return airfare between China and the UK
  • Reimbursement of one-off visa application fees

The available PhD programmes can be explored through Brunel University’s programme listings.

Scholarship Benefits

Full Tuition Fee Coverage

Brunel University of London will provide full tuition fee funding for up to 48 months for each successful scholarship recipient.

Living-Cost Stipend

The China Scholarship Council will provide a stipend to support living costs during the scholarship period.

The stipend also includes medical insurance.

International Airfare

Each scholarship recipient will receive funding for one international round-trip economy-class airfare between China and the UK.

Visa Application Fee

CSC will reimburse the successful recipient for one-off visa application fees.

PhD Study Duration

The scholarship can support PhD studies for up to 48 months.

Successful applicants are expected to commence their doctoral studies in either:

  • October 2027, or
  • January 2028

Available Fields of Study

The scholarships are available for PhD studies across all disciplines at Brunel University of London.

Applicants should explore Brunel’s available research degree programmes and identify a PhD programme that matches their academic background and proposed research interests.

Who Can Apply?

The Brunel University and CSC PhD Scholarship is specifically intended for eligible Chinese students.

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • Be a citizen of the People’s Republic of China.
  • Overseas Chinese students may be eligible depending on CSC policy applicable at the time of application.
  • Have a strong academic background.
  • Meet Brunel University’s academic entry requirements.
  • Meet Brunel University’s English language entry requirements.
  • Meet the relevant requirements of the China Scholarship Council.
  • Obtain the necessary UK visa to enter and study in the UK.

Applicants should also carefully review the CSC’s own eligibility criteria because meeting Brunel University’s requirements alone does not guarantee eligibility for CSC funding.

Current Brunel PhD Students

Current first-year PhD students at Brunel University of London may also be eligible under specific conditions.

Students who started their PhD after January 2026 can apply and will be considered by CSC in open competition alongside other applicants.

If successful, their CSC scholarship funding will begin from the second year of their PhD.

Current first-year PhD students have additional application requirements, including a short personal statement of no more than 750 words explaining their research topic and supervisor, as well as a recommendation letter from their supervisor confirming that they have successfully passed the nine-month progress review.

These materials must be submitted before the deadline to:

internationalsponsorship@brunel.ac.uk

Application Deadline

The deadline for the Brunel University of London application is:

8 January 2027 at 12:00 AM

Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the deadline.

How to Apply

The application process involves two main stages: first applying to Brunel University of London and then, if nominated, applying to the China Scholarship Council.

Step 1: Identify a Suitable Supervisor

Applicants should contact the relevant Brunel University department or academic staff member to identify a suitable PhD supervisor.

Potential supervisors and their research expertise can be explored through Brunel University’s staff directory.

Applicants should establish that their proposed research aligns with the expertise of the prospective supervisor.

Step 2: Apply for PhD Admission to Brunel

Applicants must apply online for admission to a Brunel PhD programme before 8 January 2027.

Brunel University assesses applications received by the deadline before selecting candidates for nomination to CSC.

Early application is strongly recommended.

Step 3: Select the Correct Funding Option

When completing the Brunel online application, applicants must indicate that they intend to apply for the:

BUL/CSC Joint Scholarship Scheme

In the Fees and Funding section of the application, applicants should:

  1. Select Funded.
  2. Select China Scholarship Council (CSC) as the funding option.
  3. Include the name of their potential supervisor.

This is an important part of the application process.

Step 4: Brunel Reviews Applications

Brunel University will assess applications submitted by the January deadline.

The university expects to select applicants for nomination to CSC by the end of February 2027.

Successful nominees will receive a Brunel offer letter.

Step 5: Apply to CSC

After being nominated by Brunel, successful applicants must apply directly to the China Scholarship Council during its application window.

The CSC application period is expected to take place in March 2027.

Applicants should check the official CSC website for the confirmed application dates and requirements.

Step 6: CSC Selection

Brunel expects to receive the final list of successful CSC scholarship recipients in late May or early June 2027.

Successful applicants will then proceed toward their PhD studies at Brunel.

Application Timeline

Stage Expected Date
Brunel application deadline 8 January 2027
Brunel selects CSC nominees End of February 2027
CSC application period Expected March 2027
CSC results received by Brunel Late May/Early June 2027
PhD commencement October 2027 or January 2028

Application Documents and Preparation

Applicants should prepare their PhD application carefully and ensure that their proposed research is appropriate for their selected programme and prospective supervisor.

Depending on the applicant’s circumstances, preparation may include:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Evidence of English language proficiency
  • Research proposal and related application materials
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Details of proposed research
  • Potential supervisor information
  • Brunel PhD application
  • CSC scholarship application

Applicants should follow Brunel University’s specific research degree application requirements and the CSC’s requirements separately.

Important Information for Current Brunel PhD Students

Current first-year Brunel PhD students who started after January 2026 have a separate requirement.

They must submit:

  • A personal statement of no more than 750 words
  • A description of their research subject
  • The name of their supervisor
  • A recommendation letter from their supervisor
  • Confirmation that they successfully passed the nine-month progress review

These materials should be sent to:

internationalsponsorship@brunel.ac.uk

before the application deadline.

Why Apply for This Scholarship?

The Brunel University and CSC partnership provides successful candidates with substantial financial support for doctoral study in the UK.

The combined funding package covers major study-related costs, including:

  • Tuition fees
  • Living expenses
  • Medical insurance
  • International travel
  • One-off visa application fees

The scholarship also provides an opportunity to undertake doctoral research at Brunel University of London across a wide range of disciplines.

Important Considerations

Admission Comes Before the CSC Application

Applicants must first apply to Brunel and receive an offer before applying to CSC.

Therefore, prospective applicants should begin the Brunel admission process well ahead of the January deadline.

Scholarship Selection Is Separate

Receiving a Brunel offer does not automatically mean that an applicant will receive CSC funding.

Brunel first selects applicants for nomination, after which nominated candidates submit their applications directly to CSC.

Check Both Sets of Requirements

Applicants must satisfy both:

  • Brunel University’s PhD admission requirements, and
  • China Scholarship Council eligibility requirements.

Start Early

Because applicants need to identify a supervisor, prepare a PhD application and subsequently apply to CSC if nominated, early preparation is strongly recommended.

Conclusion

The Brunel University of London and China Scholarship Council PhD Scholarship 2027/28 provides 20 fully funded PhD opportunities for eligible Chinese students seeking doctoral study in the United Kingdom.

Successful candidates can receive full tuition fee coverage for up to 48 months, a CSC living-cost stipend including medical insurance, an international round-trip economy-class flight between China and the UK, and reimbursement of one-off visa application fees.

The scholarship is open across Brunel’s PhD disciplines, with studies expected to begin in October 2027 or January 2028.

Applicants must first apply to Brunel University and obtain an offer before proceeding to the CSC application stage. The Brunel application deadline is 8 January 2027, so prospective applicants should begin identifying suitable supervisors and preparing their applications early.
