item.content:encoded:
The M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity is advancing community health equity through partnerships, research, leadership development and initiatives focused on addressing the social and structural factors that influence health outcomes.

As part of this work, M Health Fairview has announced the Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship, a year-long leadership development programme designed to support community leaders working on innovative projects that promote health equity and address the social determinants of health.

The Center works alongside community partners toward a shared goal of improving the health of the communities it serves. It is located within the Fairview Community Health and Wellness Hub and provides a space for M Health Fairview and community partners to collaborate on reducing racial and other disparities in community health outcomes.

About the M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity

The Center for Community Health Equity extends the work of M Health Fairview’s Community Advancement team.

Its approach brings together the health system, community organizations, leaders and residents to address factors that influence health beyond traditional clinical care.

The Center’s work is built around three key strategies:

1. Community Incubator

This strategy focuses on addressing the social determinants and drivers of health as well as individual social risk factors.

2. Engagement Infrastructure

The Center works to build trusting partnerships while creating opportunities for community and patient voices to inform its work.

3. Inclusive Institution

The Center also works toward transforming structures to create an increasingly equitable and inclusive environment.

Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship

The newly launched Accelerator Fellowship is a year-long leadership development programme.

The fellowship is designed to support community leaders who are advancing innovative projects focused on:

  • Health equity
  • Social determinants of health
  • Community improvement
  • Innovative community-based solutions

 

The available source introduces the fellowship but does not provide detailed information about the application deadline, number of fellows, funding amount, eligibility requirements or application procedure.

Therefore, applicants should consult the official M Health Fairview information before making assumptions about these details.

Understanding the Social Determinants of Health

M Health Fairview states that research shows 80% of health occurs outside hospitals and clinics. The organization therefore emphasizes the importance of addressing social determinants of health through enhanced models of care and service delivery.

This approach recognizes that factors outside traditional healthcare settings can influence the health and wellbeing of communities.

The Center’s initiatives address several of these broader factors.

Key Social Determinants of Health Initiatives

Food Is Medicine

The Food is Medicine initiative focuses on using food to support patients, strengthen communities and contribute to system-level change.

The initiative reflects the Center’s focus on improving access to resources that contribute to community health.

Housing Is Health

The Housing is Health initiative focuses on stable and affordable housing as an important foundation for strong communities and inclusive growth.

Connection Is Cure

The Connection is Cure initiative focuses on building trust through social connections, recognizing linguistic and cultural diversity and connecting communities with the health system.

Population Health Equity Initiatives

M Health Fairview also applies equity-centered and culturally responsive approaches to healthcare.

According to the Center, its approach involves:

  1. Identifying challenges and opportunities.
  2. Creating or expanding programmes and partnerships.
  3. Testing and developing solutions.
  4. Scaling or deepening successful approaches across the health system and communities.

 

Current population health equity initiatives include the Native Health Equity Initiative and Birth Justice Initiative.

Native Health Equity Initiative

The initiative, known as Healing in Four Directions, seeks to build trust and establish partnerships to better serve Native patients, employees and community members.

Birth Justice Initiative

The Birth Justice Initiative is a cross-departmental effort involving community members, patients, providers and employees.

It focuses on aligning and amplifying equity-driven solutions to improve outcomes for birthing individuals and their babies.

Who Is the Accelerator Fellowship For?

The information provided by M Health Fairview describes the Accelerator Fellowship as a programme for community leaders who are advancing innovative projects related to health equity and social determinants of health.

However, the available source does not specify:

  • A minimum or maximum age
  • Citizenship requirements
  • Academic requirements
  • Geographic eligibility
  • Professional experience requirements
  • Number of fellows selected
  • Whether the programme provides a stipend or grant
  • Application deadline
  • Application form or submission procedure

Prospective applicants should therefore check the official fellowship information for the latest application details.

Why the Fellowship Matters

Community health challenges often extend beyond healthcare facilities.

The Accelerator Fellowship’s focus on leadership development and innovative community projects connects directly with the Center’s broader approach of working with community partners to improve health outcomes.

The programme may therefore be relevant to community leaders developing solutions that address issues affecting health and wellbeing at the community level.

M Health Fairview’s Community-Based Approach

The Center builds on M Health Fairview’s existing partnerships with:

  • Government organizations
  • Community-based nonprofits
  • Private organizations
  • Community leaders
  • Patients and residents

The organization describes this as part of a long-standing commitment to addressing the social determinants of health.

This partnership-based approach is central to the Center’s efforts to develop and expand health equity initiatives.

Center for Community Health Equity Workgroup

The Center’s work is supported by a workgroup made up of experts from across the M Health Fairview health system.

The workgroup provides leadership and helps shape and guide the Center’s work.

Members include professionals from areas such as:

  • Family medicine
  • Health equity research
  • Health disparities research
  • Pediatrics
  • Behavioral neuroscience
  • Health informatics
  • Quality improvement
  • Community engagement
  • Inclusive excellence

How to Learn More

Individuals interested in the Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship should review the official M Health Fairview information for application details as they become available.

The Center’s official page provides additional information about its work and the Accelerator Fellowship.

Official information:
https://www.mhealthfairview.org/about-us/health-equity/m-health-fairview-center-for-community-health-equity/cche

Conclusion

The M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity brings together healthcare professionals, community partners and other stakeholders to address health disparities and the social factors that influence community health.

Its newly launched Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship provides a year-long leadership development opportunity for community leaders working on innovative projects that promote health equity and address social determinants of health.

Beyond the fellowship, the Center’s wider work includes initiatives focused on food access, housing, social connection, Native health equity and birth justice.

Prospective applicants should monitor the official M Health Fairview page for detailed fellowship eligibility, funding, application requirements and deadlines when those details are published.

Discover more fellowship opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is currently inviting applications for several opportunities across its professional, general services, short-term, consultancy and internship categories.

These openings provide opportunities for professionals and early-career applicants interested in contributing to international climate action through the UNFCCC Secretariat.

The current openings include positions in technology, mitigation, adaptation, communications and engagement, markets and non-market support, as well as other areas connected to the UNFCCC’s work.

Current UNFCCC Vacancies

The current vacancies are divided into four main categories: fixed-term employment, short-term employment, consultancy and internship opportunities.

1. Fixed-Term Employment Opportunities

Programme Officer — P-3

Programme: Technology Subdivision, Means of Implementation (MOI) Division

Level: P-3

Application Period: 11 September – 27 September 2026

Announcement Number: VA 26/041/MoI

The Programme Officer position is part of the Technology Subdivision within the Means of Implementation Division.

Interested applicants should review the official vacancy announcement for the detailed responsibilities, qualifications and application requirements.

Programme Assistant — G-5

Programme: Constituted Bodies and Data Services Subdivision, Mitigation Division

Level: G-5

Application Period: 18 September – 4 October 2026

Announcement Number: VA 26/042/M

This is a General Services position within the Mitigation Division.

Applicants should consult the official vacancy announcement for complete information about the role and required qualifications.

2. Short-Term Employment

Associate Programme Officer — P-2

Programme: Vulnerability Subdivision, Adaptation Division

Level: P-2

Application Period: 18 September – 4 October 2026

Announcement Number: 26/TJO13/A

The position is located within the Adaptation Division’s Vulnerability Subdivision.

The detailed vacancy announcement should be reviewed carefully before applying.

3. Consultancy Opportunity

Consultant — Technical Paper on Enhancing Observer Engagement

Programme: Communications & Engagement Division

Level: N/A

Application Period: 18 September – 4 October 2026

Announcement Number: 26/CON10/C&E

The consultancy supports work on a technical paper on enhancing observer engagement under SBI Arrangements for Intergovernmental Meetings.

Applicants should consult the official announcement for the complete consultancy scope, deliverables, qualifications and submission requirements.

4. Internship Opportunity

Intern — Mitigation, Markets and Non-Market Support

Programme: Mitigation, Markets and non-markets support

Level: N/A

Application Period: 24 September – 18 October 2026

Announcement Number: 25/Intern29/M-Market and non-markets support

This internship provides an opportunity for an early-career applicant to gain experience within the UNFCCC’s work on mitigation, markets and non-market approaches.

Applicants should review the official internship vacancy announcement for the complete requirements.

UNFCCC Application Deadlines

Applicants should pay close attention to the individual closing dates because each vacancy has a different application period.

Position Category Level Deadline
Programme Officer Fixed-term P-3 27 September 2026
Programme Assistant Fixed-term G-5 4 October 2026
Associate Programme Officer Short-term P-2 4 October 2026
Consultant Consultancy N/A 4 October 2026
Intern Internship N/A 18 October 2026

How to Apply for UNFCCC Vacancies

The UNFCCC states that applicants should only use its online application system when applying for vacancy announcements.

Step 1: Register

Click the Apply Now button associated with the vacancy you are interested in.

Applicants will first be asked to register as users with the UNFCCC Online Application System.

Step 2: Complete the Application

After registration, applicants can apply for a vacancy by completing their Personal History Form (P.11) through the online system.

Applicants can also save their profile so that information can be updated and used for future vacancy applications.

Step 3: Submit the Application

Applicants should carefully review their information before submitting the completed online application.

The UNFCCC advises applicants not to attach additional documents during the initial online application process.

If an applicant is invited for an interview, they may subsequently be required to provide documentary evidence supporting information included in the application.

Step 4: Check the Acknowledgement Email

After submitting an online application, applicants should receive an acknowledgement by email.

The UNFCCC states that if an acknowledgement is not received within 24 hours, applicants should contact:

vacancies@unfccc.int

Applicants who receive the automatic notification do not need to submit another application through another method.

Application Preparation Tips

Review the Specific Vacancy Announcement

Each position has its own announcement and requirements. Applicants should read the relevant vacancy announcement carefully before applying.

Prepare Your Personal History Form

The UNFCCC uses the P.11 Personal History Form as part of its online application process. Applicants should ensure that their information is accurate and complete.

Apply Before the Closing Time

Do not wait until the final hours to submit an application. Allow sufficient time for registration, completing the application and receiving the submission acknowledgement.

Check Your Email

After submitting an application, monitor the email address associated with your UNFCCC application account for the acknowledgement and any subsequent communication.

Opportunities Across Climate Action

The current UNFCCC openings cover several areas connected to international climate policy and implementation.

The vacancies span:

  • Technology
  • Means of implementation
  • Mitigation
  • Adaptation
  • Vulnerability
  • Communications and engagement
  • Observer engagement
  • Climate markets
  • Non-market approaches

This range demonstrates the variety of professional functions involved in supporting the UNFCCC’s work.

Conclusion

The UNFCCC Current Openings 2026 provide several opportunities for professionals, early-career applicants and specialists interested in contributing to international climate action.

The available positions include Programme Officer, Programme Assistant, Associate Programme Officer, Consultant and Intern opportunities across different UNFCCC divisions.

Applicants should carefully review the individual vacancy announcements, confirm that they meet the relevant requirements and submit their applications through the official UNFCCC online application system before the applicable deadline.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Center for Eastern European Studies (CEES) at the University of Zurich is inviting applications for its Spring 2027 Fellowship Program, offering 5–6 residential fellowships to highly talented and innovative young or mid-career scholars in the social sciences and humanities.

The fellowship provides an opportunity to spend up to four months in Zurich, pursue independent research, participate in the academic activities of CEES, and engage with an interdisciplinary community of scholars working on Russia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia.

About the CEES Fellowship Program

The CEES Fellowship is normally structured as a four-month residential fellowship during one academic semester.

For the Spring 2027 semester, the fellowship will begin in mid-February 2027.

The programme welcomes research proposals addressing historical or contemporary topics related to:

  • Russia
  • Eastern Europe
  • The Caucasus
  • Central Asia
  • Post-Soviet Eurasia

For the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle, CEES is particularly interested in scholars researching:

  • Geopolitical trends
  • Economic connectivity
  • Transnational social issues
  • Transnational cultural issues
  • The South Caucasus region

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship will last for up to four months, beginning in mid-February 2027.

During their residency, fellows are expected to focus on their independent research while actively participating in the scholarly activities of the Center for Eastern European Studies.

What Does the Fellowship Provide?

The CEES Fellowship provides several forms of support to selected scholars.

Living Expenses

The fellowship includes a stipend for living expenses during the fellowship period of up to four months.

Travel and Administrative Costs

Funding also covers travel and administrative costs in Switzerland.

Workspace and Facilities

Fellows receive access to:

  • A workspace at CEES
  • Relevant libraries
  • Necessary research facilities
  • The interdisciplinary academic community associated with CEES

Housing Support

CEES will assist fellows with finding housing in the Zurich area during their residency.

Research and Academic Activities

The fellowship is not solely a research stay. Fellows are expected to actively participate in the academic environment at CEES.

During the fellowship, selected scholars will:

  • Pursue independent research in residence.
  • Participate actively in CEES scholarly activities.
  • Access relevant libraries and research resources.
  • Present their research topic in a workshop.
  • Engage with the interdisciplinary community of experts associated with CEES.
  • Publish their findings through one of the CEES publication outlets.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is intended for young or mid-career scholars working in the:

  • Social sciences
  • Humanities

Applicants should have a research focus addressing historical or contemporary topics connected to Russia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus or Central Asia.

For Spring 2027, applications connected to the South Caucasus and focusing on geopolitical trends, economic connectivity, or transnational social and cultural issues are particularly welcomed.

Important Eligibility Requirement

Applicants must be enrolled or employed at their home university.

This means the fellowship is intended for scholars who maintain an academic affiliation with their home institution during the application and fellowship process.

Application Requirements

A complete application must contain all of the following materials:

1. Letter of Motivation

Applicants should submit a letter explaining their motivation for applying to the CEES Fellowship Program.

2. Research Proposal

A 3–5 page research proposal is required.

The proposal should clearly present the research project the applicant intends to pursue during the fellowship.

3. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a CV that includes a list of publications.

4. Writing Sample

Applicants should provide a short writing sample, such as an:

  • Academic article
  • Book chapter

5. CEES Presentation Proposal

Applicants must also submit a short proposal for the presentation they would give at CEES during their fellowship.

6. References

Applicants must provide two letters of recommendation and/or the names of two referees.

Language and Submission Format

All application materials must be written in English.

The complete application should be combined into one single PDF document.

Applications should be sent by email to:

cees@isos.uzh.ch

Application Deadline

The deadline for the Spring 2027 CEES Fellowship is:

12 October 2026

Applicants should ensure that the complete application reaches CEES by the stated deadline.

Fellowship Timeline

Detail Information
Fellowship CEES Fellowship Program
Semester Spring 2027
Location University of Zurich, Switzerland
Number of Fellowships 5–6
Duration Up to 4 months
Start Mid-February 2027
Target Applicants Young and mid-career scholars
Fields Social sciences and humanities
Application Language English
Deadline 12 October 2026
Application Format Single PDF
Email cees@isos.uzh.ch

Areas of Research Interest

CEES welcomes research proposals across topics related to Eastern Europe and post-Soviet Eurasia.

For this particular fellowship cycle, applicants with research interests in the South Caucasus are especially encouraged to consider the programme where their work addresses areas such as:

  • Geopolitical developments
  • Economic connectivity
  • Cross-border social dynamics
  • Transnational cultural issues

Research may focus on historical or contemporary issues within the broader geographic scope of the fellowship.

How to Apply

Interested scholars should prepare all required application materials in English and combine them into a single PDF document.

The application should contain:

  1. Letter of motivation
  2. 3–5 page research proposal
  3. CV with publication list
  4. Short writing sample
  5. Proposal for the CEES presentation
  6. Two recommendation letters and/or names of two referees

The completed PDF should then be emailed to:

cees@isos.uzh.ch

Application Preparation Tips

Applicants should ensure that their research proposal clearly demonstrates what they intend to accomplish during the four-month residency.

It is also important to ensure that the writing sample, CV and presentation proposal complement the research project described in the application.

Because the fellowship requires active participation in CEES activities, applicants should also demonstrate how their research can contribute to the Center’s interdisciplinary academic environment.

Funding

The CEES Fellowship provides financial support covering:

  • Living expenses through a stipend
  • Travel costs in Switzerland
  • Administrative costs in Switzerland

Selected fellows also receive research facilities, workspace and library access.

CEES will assist fellows in finding accommodation in the Zurich area.

About CEES

The Center for Eastern European Studies (CEES) is based at the University of Zurich and supports interdisciplinary research and scholarly exchange focused on Eastern Europe and post-Soviet Eurasia.

The CEES Fellowship Program is funded by the Department of History and supported by the University of Zurich.

Conclusion

The CEES Fellowship Program 2027 provides young and mid-career scholars in the social sciences and humanities with an opportunity to undertake independent research in residence at the University of Zurich.

The programme offers 5–6 residential fellowships lasting up to four months, with financial support for living expenses, travel and administrative costs, as well as access to research facilities and an interdisciplinary scholarly network.

Applicants working on Russia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus or Central Asia are eligible to consider the programme, with particular interest for the Spring 2027 cycle in research addressing the South Caucasus, geopolitical trends, economic connectivity and transnational social or cultural issues.

The application deadline is 12 October 2026.

Discover more fellowship opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The NFL Rotational Program 2027 offers current undergraduate seniors an opportunity to begin a full-time career with the National Football League through a highly selective, two-year rotational programme.

Participants can complete up to four project-based rotations across different NFL offices and departments, gaining experience in areas such as communications, finance, football operations, marketing, broadcasting, international business, events, media and more.

The programme offers a listed salary of $72,000 USD and is scheduled to begin in July 2027.

About the NFL Rotational Program

The NFL Rotational Program is designed to give participants broad professional experience through challenging assignments, League events and networking opportunities across different areas of the organization.

During the two-year programme, participants may complete up to four rotations depending on business needs, their performance and previous experience.

Potential locations include:

  • NFL League Office — New York
  • NFL Media — California
  • NFL Government Affairs Office — Washington, DC
  • NFL Films — New Jersey

The specific department assigned during each rotation will be determined according to the NFL’s business needs.

Departments and Areas of Work

Previous programme rotations have included a wide range of business functions, including:

  • Communications & Public Affairs
  • Events Strategy
  • Finance
  • Football Operations
  • International
  • Marketing & Sales
  • Broadcasting
  • Labor Operations
  • Media

The programme can therefore provide exposure to different aspects of professional sports operations and business.

Who Can Apply?

The NFL is considering applications from currently enrolled undergraduate seniors, including students completing a fifth consecutive year.

Applicants must:

  • Be graduating between Winter 2026 and Spring 2027.
  • Have an overall GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Be available to begin the two-year programme in July 2027.
  • Be legally permitted to work in the United States.
  • Have all required visas and U.S. employment authorizations before the programme begins if they are international students.
  • Be willing to relocate to any NFL League office for a rotation during the two-year programme.
  • Have strong internship or previous work experience.
  • Demonstrate an interest in gaining diverse professional experience within professional sports.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Applicants are expected to demonstrate strong professional and interpersonal capabilities.

The NFL lists the following qualifications and skills:

Microsoft Office

Applicants should have advanced experience using:

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Excel

Communication and Relationship Management

Candidates should demonstrate:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Strong communication skills
  • Relationship management abilities
  • Excellent presentation skills

Analytical and Organizational Skills

Applicants should also demonstrate:

  • Independent thinking
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Analytical and critical-thinking skills
  • Planning and organizational abilities
  • Strong time-management skills

Adaptability and Collaboration

Participants are expected to be able to adapt to different work environments, leadership styles and teams.

The ability to work collaboratively across functions is also required.

Programme Responsibilities

Participants will undertake project-based assignments during each rotation.

The work may involve different departments depending on the NFL’s current organizational needs and the participant’s previous experience and performance.

The rotational structure is intended to provide exposure to different professional functions rather than placing participants permanently in one department from the beginning.

Two-Year Programme Structure

The programme is a full-time two-year rotational opportunity.

Participants may complete up to four rotations during this period.

At the end of the programme, participants may choose to pursue:

  • Internal opportunities within the NFL
  • Further education
  • Opportunities with NFL Clubs
  • Opportunities with partner organizations
  • Career opportunities outside the NFL

Continued employment with the NFL after the scheduled end of the rotational programme is not guaranteed.

Work Location and Relocation

The programme requires participants to be available for onsite work.

Potential rotation locations include New York, California, Washington, DC and New Jersey.

Participants must therefore be willing to relocate to an NFL League office when required by their rotation placement.

No relocation assistance will be provided.

The position does not offer remote or hybrid working options. The NFL states that in-person work at its offices is a priority for collaboration, professional connections and organizational culture.

Working Hours

NFL employees are expected to work 40 hours per week.

Occasional travel may also be required depending on the participant’s rotation placement.

Salary

The advertised salary for the NFL Rotational Program is:

$72,000 USD

The posting indicates that the NFL expects to hire near the middle of the stated salary range. The listed salary amount is $72,000.

Applicants should also review the NFL’s official benefits information for details of its employee benefits package.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

Wednesday, September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET

Only fully completed eligible applications will be considered.

Applicants should ensure that they submit an updated resume as part of their application.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through the NFL’s official employer application portal.

Before submitting an application, candidates should ensure that they:

  1. Meet the graduation requirements.
  2. Have a minimum GPA of 3.0.
  3. Confirm their U.S. work authorization.
  4. Prepare an updated resume.
  5. Review their previous internship and work experience.
  6. Confirm their availability to begin in July 2027.
  7. Be prepared to relocate for different rotations.
  8. Submit the completed application before the deadline.

Official Application: NFL Careers – Rotational Program

What the NFL Looks For

Beyond the formal qualifications, the NFL describes several attributes expected of employees.

These include:

  • An enthusiastic and proactive attitude
  • Willingness to learn
  • Strong work ethic
  • Adaptability
  • Relationship-building skills
  • Ability to influence and collaborate
  • Resilience and persistence
  • Passion for professional growth

The NFL also identifies leadership attributes such as building talent, executing effectively, inspiring others, living organizational values, understanding the business and thinking ambitiously.

Important Considerations for Applicants

1. Confirm Your Graduation Date

The programme is specifically aimed at students graduating between Winter 2026 and Spring 2027.

2. Check Your Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. International students must have the necessary visas and U.S. employment authorizations before the programme begins.

3. Prepare an Updated Resume

The NFL specifically states that only fully completed eligible applications will be considered and requires an updated resume.

4. Be Prepared to Relocate

Rotation placement can require relocation to different NFL offices, so applicants should consider this requirement before applying.

5. Apply Before the Deadline

Applications close at 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2026.

Conclusion

The NFL Rotational Program 2027 provides graduating undergraduate students with a structured opportunity to gain professional experience across multiple areas of the National Football League.

The two-year programme can include up to four rotations across NFL offices and departments, with project-based assignments, networking opportunities and exposure to different areas of professional sports operations.

Eligible students graduating between Winter 2026 and Spring 2027 with a GPA of at least 3.0 should review the requirements carefully and submit a complete application before the September 30, 2026 deadline.
